restrictions: Target sha256-r39-prefix-v1: SHA-256 steps 0..38 on every padded block, the standard IV once, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all eight digest words; output two distinct 128-byte messages M0 || M1 and M0 || M1' with equal digests.

Construction: differential attack using the claw construction for row 16 (solving W16 = K(a0, cv) + f(u) via a van Oorschot-Wiener collision search), a 1 MiB DFS dense-base solver, and the published 39-step characteristic (ePrint 2026/1120, Table 21) with the accepted event relaxing row 20 to signed differences.

Cost: time 2^123.39 target compressions (C = 2812). Claw-search kernel counted at 70 operations per 7 lanes; evaluations per claw 2^11.41 (conservative by 0.441 bits against the schedule of proof.md Appendix E.3); per-claw success probability 2^-120.71 = side conditions 2^-10.44 (the exact product 2^-9.81 LESS the 0.63-bit adverse deviation measured at a 24-bit prefix, charged not disclosed), row 17 2^-32, tail rows 18+ 2^-78.273 (a 99% bootstrap lower bound with Bonferroni 8 on the arithmetic mean of a pooled 140-seed study, stalls entered as zero, less 0.52 bits for estimator bias). Score under hashsmash-scalar-tm-v1: 123.39 + max(0, 21 - 20) = 124.39, ahead of our accepted generic entry 744875ec at 124.83147 by 0.44 bits.

Success probability at least 0.39 under H2, H3, H4, H6, H8, H9, H11, H12 and H13. All eight are score-critical. H12, the uniform-expansion premise, carries 78.27 of the 120.71 per-claw bits and was undeclared before this filing.

Memory 2^21 bytes. Dense solver: 1,048,576 linear + 94,483 module = 1,143,059. Claw search: 1,600,000 DP table (128,000 slots at 12.5 bytes) + ~60,000 code + ~2,000 condition tables + ~1,200 state + 3,800 advice (the full advice envelope of restrictions[6], not the 1,024 bytes of bases alone, which earlier filings used here) = 1,667,000 peak. The filed 2^21 = 2,097,152 is an envelope over the larger of the two sequential phases, with 430,152 bytes of headroom. Score under hashsmash-scalar-tm-v1: 123.39 + max(0, 21 - 20) = 124.39.

Reconstruction: the complete characteristic and its 140 bit conditions (Appendix A), the filed dense base b1 (B), the dense solver level by level (C), the tail estimator and the limits of its reported bound (D), the claw search, its measured rate curve, its chaining-value schedule and how collision resolution is batched and priced (E), the emitted packed kernel (F), the probability space including the a0-even/u-odd restriction (G), and what each experiment does and does not establish (H) are all in proof.md.

Advice: nonuniform_advice_log2_bytes = 12 covers the four dense bases (1,024 bytes) together with the published characteristic the attack consumes as fixed non-derived data (23 row records and 140 bit conditions, about 1,700-2,800 bytes), total 2,700-3,800 bytes. Earlier filings charged 10, counting the bases only. preprocessing_log2 = 40 covers the audited 496-CPU-hour campaign of restrictions[13] -- the characteristic work and the re-solution of rows 0..3 that produced b1 -- and NOT the dense-base DFS of Section 4, which Appendix B.1 establishes did not produce the filed base. An earlier version of this restriction said the opposite, that preprocessing covered the DFS alone and excluded the characteristic search; that was stale against Appendix B.1 and is withdrawn. What is NOT claimed is that this campaign bounds the published authors' own search; see premise H13.

Declared heuristics are H2, H3, H4, H6, H8, H9, H11, H12 and H13. There is no H5: it was a tail-transfer premise retired when the tail was measured directly on the filed base. H1 is retired because the ledger does not use it. H10 is disclosed in proof.md Section 9 but constrains no ledger term and is not declared. The numbering is kept so that earlier review findings remain legible.

Provenance of the filed base: b1 is the published base of Appendix A.4 with rows 0..3 re-solved, not an independent output of the dense solver; 48 of the 72 compared registers over rows 0..15 are bit-for-bit identical and the 24 that differ are exactly those the SHA-256 relations force. Consequently preprocessing_log2 = 40 is a conservative upper bound rather than a measurement of the work behind b1, and the unrelaxed tail cross-check is withdrawn as circular. Appendix B.1 records this; it does not affect correctness, since b1 satisfies every state and schedule relation for both members and admits rows 16 and 17.

Claw-selected measurement: the per-claw factors are no longer evaluated only on uniform words. experiments/clawdist.py constructs genuine claws through the filed walk function and the base b1 schedule, confirms that every claw has a0 even and u odd, and measures the side-condition rates and the low-bit distribution of W17 on them. The tail remains the factor not measured under that distribution.

Retired heuristics: H1 and H5 are both withdrawn and the numbering is kept so earlier review findings remain legible. H5 was a tail-transfer premise, unnecessary once the tail was measured directly on the filed base. H1 asserted that the fixed target g is at least as good as a random one; no ledger line consumes it, because every per-claw factor is evaluated at g -- the row-17 term is the exact |G17(g)| = 1, the tail study's row-16/17 stages select g and condition on it, and the side conditions are measured on claw-selected variants that target g. There is no random-target quantity anywhere to transfer, so the premise is removed rather than defended.

Two premises that earlier filings asserted are now measured by organizer-run experiments: the splitting estimator's bias (splitting-bias-r39, against a toy with an exactly known answer) and the side-condition factorization under claw selection (the prefix ladder in claw-selected-factors-r39). Two experiments whose checks were identities, clawexp.py and jointside.py, are withdrawn; the algebraic fact jointside.py restated is now a theorem in proof.md rather than an experiment.

Yield of a fixed work budget: the ledger charges an average claw rate. The single-window yield is measured directly -- each vow-rate-stability-r39 trial is one fixed budget, giving 256 samples with mean 8.66 claws, sd 2.96, cv 0.342, first percentile 3 -- so a single window's lower tail is real. It cannot affect the attack: the schedule sums 2^104.21 independent windows, so the relative standard deviation of the total is 0.342 / sqrt(2^104.21) = 2^-53.7, concentrated 48 bits below any precision this ledger reports. Charging the average rate is therefore correct by concentration, not by assumption (proof.md Appendix E.4).

Preprocessing: charged from an audited wall-clock budget. Our 39-step campaign over the published message shape is logged job by job (52 jobs: 34 UNSAT, 4 SAT, 14 TIMEOUT at a 4-hour cap, 55.5 CPU-hours); all 124 job specifications at the full cap give 496 CPU-hours, covering both the characteristic search and the re-solution of rows 0..3 that produced b1. The dense-solver DFS of Section 4 is NOT charged here: Appendix B.1 establishes it did not produce the filed base.

Preprocessing, conversion insensitivity: converting wall-clock at R primitive operations per core-second gives 2^39.21 at R = 10^9, 2^45.85 at 10^11, 2^59.14 at 10^15 and 2^75.75 at 10^20. The filed time_log2 = 123.39 is unchanged for any construction cost below 2^115.26, so R would have to exceed 10^31.9 before the exponent moved; the conversion rate is therefore not load-bearing. preprocessing_log2 = 40 is the figure at R = 10^9, reported because the field requires a number. We do not claim our campaign bounds the authors' search; 14 of our jobs hit the cap undecided.

heuristics.statement: Each chaining value is run for 2^26 trail evaluations and then abandoned for a fresh first block, at which point its measured rate is 2^10.972 evaluations per distinct claw. The ledger nevertheless charges 2^11.414, the cumulative rate of a single 2^30-evaluation run, and the premise is that this charged rate is attainable at the 2^104.21 chaining values the attack needs.
heuristics.scope: The evaluations-per-claw term in the time ledger. The charged figure is conservative with respect to the schedule actually specified: the schedule supports 2^10.972 and the ledger charges 2^11.414, a margin of 0.441 bits that is not taken.
heuristics.extrapolation: The measured curve is reproduced in full in proof.md Appendix E.2. Its marginal rate falls to 2^10.878 by 2^25 trail evaluations and then climbs steadily to 2^11.644 by 2^30: a single chaining value's graph has only 2^32 points and the search begins re-covering ground, which is depletion. The earlier filing asserted that the saturated rate was stable over the latter part of that run; the data contradicts that and the claim is withdrawn. The schedule of Appendix E.3 avoids the depleted regime by switching chaining value at the minimum of the curve, so the quantity carried to full scale is a short-run rate rather than a long-run one. Per-window overheads are negligible: clearing the 128000-slot table costs 2^-9.50 operations per evaluation and regenerating the constants less still.
heuristics.limitations: One chaining value's functional graph was measured, over a 2^30-evaluation run that is not in the package. The premise is that a 2^26-evaluation window behaves at the remaining 2^104.21 chaining values as it does at this one; no distribution over graphs is established. The reduced-scale experiment runs a 2^20 domain with a substituted even branch and, over its three-fold span, has little power to detect depletion at the rates Appendix E.2 measures; it shows the search executes and is steady at that scale, nothing more.

heuristics.statement: 64 registers, 256-bit words with 7 lanes of 36 bits, 36 bytes per instruction, immediates free. Same convention as 744875ec. The kernel uses 7 peak live registers.
heuristics.scope: The operations-per-evaluation term. C = 2812 word operations per 39-step compression. The claw kernel costs 70 operations per 7-lane word (10.0 per lane evaluation) plus overhead of 23 operations (rounded up from estimated 22.4).
heuristics.extrapolation: The kernel is counted instruction by instruction by a tracer that is now inside the package: experiments/kernelcount.py rebuilds it on every organizer trial, counts 70 operations for 7 lanes with peak live registers 7, and checks the emitted program against an independent scalar implementation on all 7 lanes of 48 packed vectors per trial with no mismatch. The emitted program is listed line by line in proof.md Appendix F. The overhead (DP test and loop, 6 operations; handler amortized at dp_bits = 7, 16.4 operations) is estimated, not traced.
heuristics.limitations: The convention is self-declared, as in 744875ec. The kernel itself is now traced by an organizer-run experiment, but the 23 operations of DP test, loop and handler overhead are estimated rather than traced and are 25% of the charge; a full trace could move the score by 0.1-0.3 bits. Larger and untested: the 7-way lane packing is worth log2 7 = 2.81 bits against the organizer's scalar price, and that credit rests entirely on the declared convention.

heuristics.statement: The tail of 2^-78.273 is a 99% bootstrap lower bound, carrying a Bonferroni factor of 8 for the row-20 selection, on the ARITHMETIC mean of the per-seed q estimates from a pooled 140-seed study on base b1 with DIFFROW=20, with all 20 stalled seeds entered as zero and 0.52 bits subtracted for estimator bias; and this applies when W16 and W17 are fixed by the claw construction.
heuristics.scope: The tail term in the per-claw success probability, 78.27 of the 120.71 per-claw bits. The statistic is the arithmetic mean of the 140 per-seed estimates, because the attack succeeds about N*E[q] times over N claws, so the Poisson formula takes E[q]. The 20 stalled seeds enter at zero, which no estimate can fall below, so the bound uses no censoring rule and no imputation. On the linear scale the stall treatment is worth 0.000384 bits (ceiling vs zero), which is why the censoring rule an earlier review objected to is no longer load-bearing. The 0.52 bits subtracted for bias is the calibration toy's exact bias at population 10, the largest population tested.
heuristics.extrapolation: 120 seeds were run under a written pre-registration and pooled with the original 20. All 140 values are in proof.md Appendix D.2, so the bound is recomputable: 400,000 resamples at seed 20261017 give 2^-141.734 (percentile) and 2^-141.753 (basic); the more conservative is taken. No new measurement was run for this filing; the seeds, estimator and stall cap are identical to cfe5c4e2 and only the statistic changed. THE BIAS ALLOWANCE IS THIS PREMISE'S WEAKEST STEP AND IS STATED AS SUCH. Earlier versions justified 0.52 bits as a 25-fold conservatism, the study running at population 2000 against a toy tested at 10-80. The filed data contradict that: the 120 completed seeds have sd(log2 q-hat) = 1.257 bits where seven fixed-effort stages at a true population of 2000 would give about sqrt(7/2000)/ln2 = 0.085, implying an EFFECTIVE population near 9.2 - the same regime the 0.52 was measured in. There is no 25-fold margin; at matched effective population the allowance is approximately the bias itself. Further, the toy's four stages are independent of the state, so its splitting population cannot degenerate, and population degeneracy is the dominant bias mechanism of a multilevel splitting estimator. What 0.52 bits bounds is the ratio-estimator component; the degeneracy component is unmeasured and unbounded by this package.
heuristics.limitations: 78.27 of the 120.71 per-claw bits, and only the first stage is measured in the package: tail-row18-r39 reaches row 18, while rows 19 through 23 and the run to row 38 remain reported rather than executed. The per-stage conditionals are not filed, so only the bootstrap step is auditable, not the per-seed estimates. The conversion from a bound on E[q-hat] to a bound on q rests on the bias allowance described under extrapolation, whose dominant mechanism is unmeasured; a reader who judges the true bias to exceed 0.52 bits by more than 0.44 should read this entry as NOT ahead of 744875ec. All 20 stalls occur at row 21, immediately after the relaxed row 20, which may mean the relaxation defers difficulty; entering them at zero is agnostic about this. The tail is also not evaluated under the claw-selected, parity-restricted distribution, and the separate premise that the attack's claw-induced expansion behaves as the estimator's free uniform proposals is declared as H12.

heuristics.statement: The N = 2^119.70 generated claws behave as sufficiently independent Bernoulli trials for the Poisson success formula, with per-claw probability p = 2^-120.71.
heuristics.scope: The conversion from per-claw probability to total work via Poisson amplification. The Poisson model requires that per-claw successes are approximately independent.
heuristics.extrapolation: Claws from different chaining values come from different walk functions; within a window the 2^15.49 claws share one. Dependence within a window is now measured rather than left open: each trial of claw-selected-factors-r39 derives its own chaining value, no duplicate claw is produced (distinct_claws equals claws in every trial), and the per-trial side-condition successes show no overdispersion against the independent binomial model, the dispersion index being about 1.04 with a standard deviation near 0.09, so clustering above roughly 30% would have shown. The uniformity of W17 under claw selection, which the -32 term rests on, is also binned there.
heuristics.limitations: The measurement is within a window and at this scale: 256 chaining values, about 1,000 claws, and a dispersion test that resolves clustering above roughly 30% and no finer. It does not bound dependence across the 2^104.21 windows the attack consumes, nor heterogeneity between walk functions, and no analysis of the success event's covariance at full scale is supplied. The Poisson conversion is near-linear in N*p at the filed value, so a variance inflation would inflate the required N roughly proportionally.

heuristics.statement: Under the claw-selected, parity-restricted distribution the two side conditions factorize at full 32-bit width. The ledger does NOT use the exact product 2^-9.808: it charges 2^-10.44, the product less the 0.63-bit adverse deviation measured at a 24-bit prefix.
heuristics.scope: The 9.81-bit side-condition term of the per-claw exponent.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured on prefixes, where it resolves: claw-selected-factors-r39 finds the joint prefix rate agreeing with the product of the marginal prefix rates to -0.43 bits at 16 bits and -0.63 at 24 bits, inside resolutions of 0.22 and 0.36. Under uniform (a0, a1) the factorization is exact, since W8 = C(a1) - a0 makes W8 uniform and independent of a1 for every fixed a1. The extrapolation is from 24-bit prefixes under claw selection, plus exactness under the uniform distribution, to full width under claw selection.
heuristics.limitations: Measured on 16- and 24-bit prefixes under claw selection: the joint rate falls BELOW the product of the marginals by 0.43 and 0.63 bits, each about twice its own quoted resolution (0.22, 0.36), both adverse, magnitude growing with prefix width. Earlier filings described these as 'inside resolutions', which the numbers do not support; that description is withdrawn. The ledger now charges the larger measured deviation. Read as a trend to full width the deviation would be nearer 0.8 bits, so a real full-width effect would cost a further 0.17 bits against a 0.44-bit margin. The full 32-bit joint has expected count under 2 on the claws the sandbox affords and is not measured. Under uniform (a0, a1) the factorization is exact since W8 = C(a1) - a0, but that is not the distribution the attack samples.

heuristics.statement: Under the claw-selected distribution the fully determined word W17 is uniform over all 32 bits, so |G17(g)| = 1 yields exactly 2^-32 for the row-17 term.
heuristics.scope: The 32-bit row-17 term of the per-claw exponent. |G17(g)| = 1 is exact and verified; this premise is about the denominator, the distribution of W17 over claws.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured on the low 6 bits: claw-selected-factors-r39 bins W17 over claws and the pooled chi-square is consistent with uniform. The extrapolation is from 6 bits to 32.
heuristics.limitations: The test has little power -- at its band it would miss an eightfold inflation of a single low-bit class about 93% of the time -- and the preimage table confines u to the 2^21 smallest odd values, so any structure in the high bits of W17 is exactly where the test does not look. This is 32 of the 120.71 bits of the per-claw exponent and is a premise, not a measurement, at full width.

heuristics.statement: After conditioning on a genuine claw and on the two side conditions, the row-17 and tail events keep the marginal probabilities the ledger uses, so the three factors may be multiplied into 2^-120.71.
heuristics.scope: The factorization of the per-claw exponent into its three groups. H8 covers the two side conditions against each other and H9 the uniformity of W17; this is the remaining premise, that the groups do not interact.
heuristics.extrapolation: Two conditioning checks on genuine claws, both low-powered and both consistent with independence. W18 from the real expansion on each claw is uniform in its low 6 bits (pooled chi-square z about -1.1), which tests the estimator's uniform-expansion premise at the first tail row under the attack's own distribution. Among claws passing the first side condition, W17's low bit is set 36 times in 85 (z about -1.4). The extrapolation is from these to the full joint event through row 38.
heuristics.limitations: Neither check reaches the tail: conditioning it on side-condition selection needs claws that also pass row 17, costing 2^-32, unreachable at sandbox scale. The W17 check sees one bit on 85 claws and would miss a shift below roughly 20%; the W18 check sees 6 bits of 32. The untested tail carries 78.27 of the 120.71 per-claw bits, so a correlation there moves the exponent one-for-one.

heuristics.statement: The frequency of the rows-18-to-38 event over the attack's claw-induced variants equals the frequency measured by an estimator that proposes W18..W23 as six free, independent, uniform 32-bit words and expands rows 24..38 from those proposals.
heuristics.scope: The whole 78.27-bit tail factor, 65% of the per-claw exponent. The estimator of proof.md Appendix D draws a parent and proposes W_r uniformly at rows 18..23. The attack has no such freedom: once a claw (a0, u) is fixed, every expanded word from W16 on is a deterministic function of (a0, u, cv), as Appendix G states. This premise is the transfer between the two measures.
heuristics.extrapolation: From a 192-bit free-word model to a population of at most 2^64 variants per chaining value, of which about 2^30 are claws, across 2^104.21 chaining values. This is the standard message-freedom modelling assumption of differential cryptanalysis and nothing in the package contradicts it, but it is an assumption about the SHA-256 message expansion rather than a measurement. Earlier filings left it undeclared, mentioned only in passing inside H11's extrapolation field; an adversarial review named it and it is declared here.
heuristics.limitations: Nothing in the package tests it as such. The nearest evidence is H11's check that W18 taken from the real expansion is uniform in its low 6 bits (pooled chi-square z about -1.1), which is one marginal on one of six words and says nothing about independence across rows or from the state reached at row 17, and whose claws come from a preimage table confining u to the 2^21 smallest odd values. It carries the tail one-for-one on the exponent against a 0.44-bit margin.

heuristics.statement: The audited 496-CPU-hour campaign, converted at an assumed rate of 10^9 primitive operations per core-second, upper-bounds the construction work charged for this attack: the characteristic work and the re-solution of rows 0..3 that produced the filed base b1. It does NOT bound the search by which the published characteristic of ePrint 2026/1120 was originally found.
heuristics.scope: preprocessing_log2 = 40. The budget is auditable as wall-clock: 52 logged jobs (34 UNSAT, 4 SAT, 14 TIMEOUT at a four-hour cap, 55.5 CPU-hours), with all 124 job specifications charged at the full cap to give 496 CPU-hours. 496 h x 10^9 ops/s / 2812 = 2^39.21, filed up at 2^40. The dense-base DFS of Section 4 is not charged here, because Appendix B.1 establishes it did not produce b1.
heuristics.extrapolation: Two steps are assumed rather than audited. First, wall-clock to primitive operations: the campaign was not instrumented at the operation level, so the conversion uses an assumed rate. Second, that our campaign's budget covers the construction the attack actually needs. Neither is a measurement. What makes them non-load-bearing is the insensitivity table of proof.md Section 7: the filed time_log2 = 123.39 is unchanged for any construction cost below 2^115.26 target compressions, so the assumed rate would have to exceed 10^31.9 operations per core-second -- some twenty-one orders of magnitude beyond any processor that exists -- before the filed exponent moved. The reported 2^40 is the figure at 10^9 and is reported because the field requires a number.
heuristics.limitations: This premise is declared because an adversarial review and the organizer's own cost lane both extracted it as an undeclared implicit assumption and rated it unsupported. It is unsupported as an audited operation count and is not claimed otherwise: there is no instrumented primitive-operation count for the campaign, 14 of our 52 logged jobs hit the four-hour cap undecided, and the filing explicitly does not claim that our campaign bounds the original authors' search for the published characteristic. What is claimed is narrower: that no plausible accounting of construction, at any conversion rate that could be argued, reaches 2^115.26 target compressions and therefore none changes the filed time. A reviewer who rejects the insensitivity argument should treat preprocessing_log2 = 40 as unaudited rather than as an established bound.
